## Summary

- Record the NeMo 26.10 container as the BAGEL card's `base_container`; the previously recorded container cannot run the BAGEL leaves at the pinned commits.
- Make `fd8ab826` the card-wide `bridge_commit` (the previous default predates BAGEL support) and drop the now-redundant leaf overrides. This also moves `pretrain_fsdp` onto a usable commit.
- Refresh `hf_to_megatron_gpu`, `pretrain.H100` and `pretrain_fsdp.H100` from new runs of the card commands on that container (no extra package installs), update the summary to the current performance-disclaimer wording, and regenerate the catalog docs.

## Known gaps

- The GPU import needs the official BAGEL checkout importable in the worker; `convert.sh` has no option for this, so it cannot be expressed in the card command.

## Verification

- `validate_card.py`: valid.
- `hf_to_megatron_gpu`: fresh one-GPU reload of the imported checkpoint has no missing/unexpected keys; all 1,223 EMA tensors exactly match after undoing the QKV/GLU fusion, including the 56 input-norm sentinels.
- `generate_model_verification_catalog.py --check` and `tests/unit_tests/doc_consistency/test_model_verification_catalog.py`: pass.

- **NVBug:** 6964569.

**Blocking — retain lossless reload verification for the refreshed import.** The replacement check only establishes tensor count, BF16 dtype, and finiteness. A checkpoint with the same 943 tensors but one finite weight changed to zero satisfies that description, although the imported model is wrong. The [previous result](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/53c45bd930b1dda1c285044978df5e90a390aab1/examples/model_verification_cards/bagel/card.yaml#L68-L74) explicitly checked a clean model reload and exact values for all 56 MoT input-norm sentinels; this refresh removes those assertions. The trusted card guidance requires reloaded keys, shapes, dtypes, and values to match for lossless conversion.

The importer's reported 943 targets do not replace this check: [BagelBridge](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/0d070b9f1e7abc9956fbb4ea66919773fd80d6f3/src/megatron/bridge/models/bagel/conversion.py#L103-L116) reports initialization coverage before [the GPU backend saves the checkpoint](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/0d070b9f1e7abc9956fbb4ea66919773fd80d6f3/scripts/conversion/gpu_backend.py#L297-L310).

**Correction:** perform a fresh one-GPU model reload of this run's saved checkpoint and compare its complete mapped tensor state with the pinned EMA, accounting for the expected BF16 cast and QKV/GLU layout mapping. Record the observed keys/shapes/dtypes/value result here and regenerate both guides and the catalog. Preserve both understanding and generation input norms—the [serialization repair explicitly covers both](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/0d070b9f1e7abc9956fbb4ea66919773fd80d6f3/src/megatron/bridge/models/bagel/provider.py#L42-L68)—alongside the neighboring attention, MLP, vision, and diffusion tensors. No post-save verifier implementation is included in this change, so an exact verifier patch cannot be inferred safely.

**Acceptance (proposed, not executed):** a clean reload has no missing/unexpected model keys, all mapped shapes and BF16 values match, and all 56 input-norm sentinels match their corresponding EMA branches. Deliberately alter one finite tensor in a test artifact and require the value check to fail; finiteness alone must not pass it.

Addressed in bd539ed8750caa1c7382e1506cc96b496060506d. I re-ran the card's `hf_to_megatron_gpu` import (Bridge at `fd8ab826`, NeMo 26.10 container). Then, in a fresh process on one GPU, I reloaded the saved checkpoint with `load_megatron_model` and compared the full tensor state with the pinned `ema.safetensors`:

- **Clean reload:** the distributed checkpoint load (strictness `return_all`) reported 0 missing and 0 unexpected keys, and `load_state_dict` reported 0 missing and 0 unexpected keys. All 943 checkpoint tensors matched the model's keys (943/943) with no shape mismatches, and every tensor in both the checkpoint and the reloaded model is BF16.
- **Values:** every reloaded tensor was mapped back to the EMA names. The fused QKV tensors were split back into Q/K/V using the group-interleaved layout (28 heads, 4 groups, head dim 128), and the GLU `linear_fc1` was split into gate and up (ffn 18944). All 1,223 EMA tensors were covered. They are already BF16, so the expected BF16 cast is the identity. 1,223/1,223 were exactly equal under `torch.equal`, with 0 mismatches. All 943 Megatron targets were checked, and no model parameter was left unchecked.
- **Sentinels:** all 56 input norms (28 understanding plus 28 generation) were exactly equal.
- **Negative control:** I changed one finite element in the reloaded model. In `layers.0.input_layernorm_moe_gen.weight` the value check failed (max abs diff 0.998) and passed again after the element was restored. In `layers.5.self_attn.k_proj.weight`, reached through the fused QKV, the check also failed (max abs diff 0.51). Finiteness alone does not pass the check.

The card's `hf_to_megatron_gpu` result now records this, and both guides and the catalog have been regenerated.
